SEND - Special Educational Needs & Disabilities
At the Federation of Bursledon Infant and Junior Schools we welcome all children and follow the local authority admissions guidance for children including those with additional needs. All staff and governors share the responsibility to ensure that the needs of all pupils are met within the Federation. The Special Educational Needs Co-ordinators (SENDCOs), Miss Becky Rider and Miss Cheryl Millington are responsible for monitoring and co-ordinating provision for pupils with special educational needs across the federation. The SENDCOs meets regularly with the Headteacher and class teachers, as well as liaising with parents and outside agencies to review the provision and progress for pupils with special educational needs. Our SENDCOs can be contacted via the school office or by emailing info@bursledonschools.co.uk.
We also have SEND support assistants who liaise with outside agencies such as Speech Therapists and Physiotherapists, and an Autism Ambassador, Mrs Holly Radford, who offers support and training for pupils, parents and staff.
Further information about our provision for pupils with SEND can be found in the policy section of our website and in our local offer (see link below).

Bursledon C of E (C) Infant Bursledon (CA) Junior Schools
Breakfast Club
Welcome to Bursledon Schools Breakfast Club. We have been running our successful breakfast club for many years now. The aim of it is to support pupils with a positive start to the day which is based on a flexible approach for parents/carers.
Places must be booked in advance via School Spider. However, if you have never booked for breakfast club before you must complete the attached registration form and return to the school office. You will then be given access to book via School Spider and also to confirm any additional details that might be required such as dietary needs.
Breakfast Club Registration Form
The clubs for both schools are combined and are run together in the junior school hall.
The club runs from 7.45am until the start of the school day. It is £4.50 per session.
The club is managed by staff already employed in both our schools and they have excellent relationships and knowledge of the pupils.
Entry to the juniors is via the main front office door, where you and your child will be greeted by a staff member, and again please ensure your child is registered with staff before you leave. Your child will then be welcomed by a member of staff and offered breakfast.
Breakfast consists of fresh juice, tea, milk, cereals, toast, and quite often pancakes or waffles.
If you want your child to have breakfast at the club, please ensure they arrive before 08.15am - after this time we are not able to provide food.
Also it is vitally important that you advise us of any allergies or intolerances that your child may have. We appreciate that you will probably already have told the school about this, and they will have let breakfast club staff know. However, to be absolutely safe, we would like you to talk to our breakfast club staff too about any issues that could affect your child.
After they have eaten, the children are then free to play in the hall - there are a range of activities to engage them with and we buy additional games or resources based on the children's interests.
At 8.30 the infant school pupils are escorted safely from the juniors directly into the rear of the infant school where they will be handed over to their respective teachers. The junior school pupils are allowed to leave the junior hall and make their way to their own classes as that time.
Breakfast club sessions must be booked and paid for in advance otherwise your child will not be allowed to attend. We have a number of ways that you can pay:
Windmills (After school club)
We are a club run by school staff and will follow the school’s values of love, respect, aspire. Offering a 2 tier school care option:
3:00-4:45pm, without dinner £8.00
3:00-6:00pm, with dinner £12.00
You will be able to book your child into the option you prefer on School Spider.
After School Club begins when school ends and runs up until 6pm. The club will operate five days a week, term time only. The club runs from the Infant hall, with junior school children being escorted from their school to the infants at the end of the school day. Parents can collect from the after-school club at any time from school finish until 6pm. Your child will not be able to leave with anyone that is not listed as a collector.
Windmills contact number (for use after 4pm) - 07516 051554

Sports Premium
What is the Sports Premium?
The Sport Premium is allocated to schools in order to improve the provision of PE and School Sport, and ensure that pupils may lead healthier lifestyles.
What is the purpose of this funding?
Schools must spend the additional funding on improving their provision of PE and sport, but they will have the freedom to choose how they do this.

Bursledon C of E (C) Infant Bursledon (CA) Junior Schools
Attendance
At The Federation of Bursledon Schools, we are committed to establishing a safe, nurturing and stimulating learning environment, where the education and welfare of pupils is given the highest priority.
For a child to reach their full educational potential a high level of attendance is essential. Parents/carers and teachers share the responsibility for supporting and promoting excellent school attendance and punctuality for all.
Good attendance is important because:
It is important that you are on time for your child’s year group start time. Registration takes place in the first 10 minutes of the day and then closes 20 minutes later. If a child arrives after this time it will be recorded as an unauthorised absence.
For all year groups across the Federation, the gates open in the morning at 8.30am and close at 8.40am. Anyone arriving after this time will need to enter school via the office in the Hub and will be recorded as late.
Our Infant School day finishes at 3:05pm and the Junior School at 3.10pm.
You must phone school to inform us if your child is too ill to attend school. If we do not receive a call from you, we will contact you. If we are unable to make contact with you, we will attempt to make contact with other emergency contacts you have given us. If we are still unable to make any contact we will make a home visit. Only genuine absence will be authorised. You will be required to provide medical evidence/certificates if your child has a poor attendance record.
See the chart below if you are unsure if you should send your child to school.
Medical Appointments
If possible you must ensure that medical appointments are made outside of school time.
Holidays are no longer authorised in term time. If you have a special circumstance you can ask the school office for a Leave of Absence Form. Each case will be reviewed independently. Please be aware if days are unauthorised this could result in a penalty notice being requested. Failure to pay can result in court action.
There is a lot of helpful information in our Attendance Policy.

Bursledon C of E (C) Infant Bursledon (CA) Junior Schools
E-Safety
At Bursledon Federation, we are committed to ensuring that every child develops the knowledge and confidence to stay safe in an increasingly digital world. Online safety is an essential part of our curriculum, and we embed it throughout our computing, PSHE, and wider learning. Alongside this ongoing teaching, we also dedicate focused E‑Safety weeks each year. During these times, pupils revisit key messages about responsible online behaviour, how to recognise risks, and what steps to take if they ever feel unsure or unsafe online.
We recognise that keeping children safe online is a shared responsibility between school and home. To support parents and carers, we provide access to a range of trusted resources offering practical advice, up‑to‑date guidance, and answers to common questions about online safety. These resources are designed to empower families to have open conversations, set clear expectations, and create safe digital environments at home.
Useful Links for Parents and Carers
Below are some helpful websites you may find valuable in supporting your child online:
Barnardo’s A clear, parent‑friendly guide to common online concerns and how to support children effectively.Keeping children safe online - Parent’s questions answered | Barnardo's (barnardos.org.uk)
Safer Internet Creating a safer internet for children
NSPCCNSPCC keeping safe online
Our Commitment to High‑Quality E‑Safety Education

This partnership ensures that our whole school community benefits from expert knowledge, consistent messaging, and a proactive approach to digital safeguarding.

Bursledon C of E (C) Infant Bursledon (CA) Junior Schools
The School Day
The school gates open at 8.30am and class teachers are then available either on the playground, or at your child's classroom door should you have any quick messages or questions. Children are welcome to go into their classrooms from 8.30am onwards.
Once children are in their classrooms, they are registered promptly and settle quickly into morning routines, including working on key skills, small group teaching interventions or 1:1 sessions. It is therefore essential that children arrive at school on time. Children arriving after the gates have been closed at 8:40am need to enter school via the infant or junior main entrance where a member of the school office team will be at the door and mark them as late, take their lunch order if applicable. If a child arrives late and there is no longer a member of office staff on the door, they will then need to be taken to the Hub.
Children have a break in the morning session. We welcome children to bring a healthy snack in to eat during breaktime. If your child is in the infant school, a piece of fruit/vegetable is provided for them on a daily basis which is funded by the government.
Children in the Junior School are welcome to bring in a snack from home. This must be a healthy snack such as fruit/vegetable/cereal bar. Sweets and chocolate are not permitted. Please remember our schools are nut and kiwi free.
Year 1 - Year 6 12:00 - 12:45
End of the school day
The total school hours per week is 32.55 hours a week for the Infant School and 33.20 for the Junior School.

Bursledon C of E (C) Infant Bursledon (CA) Junior Schools
EYFS
Welcome to our information page for Early Years Foundation Stage classes - also know as our Reception Classes; Dolphins Class, Octopus Class and Rainbow Fish Class.
New to our school? Below you find the links to some important forms that need to be completed when your child joins Bursledon Infant School in one of our Reception classes.
Click here for our EYFS policy.
Click here for our EYFS vision statement.
We can now put on our wellies and coats so we can go out and explore the field and woodland. The children have loved the rainy weather as they have been finding big puddles to jump in!
We have been developing our listening skills to help us get ready to learn letter sounds.
We are learning to recognise and write our names. We use the pencil rap to help us hold our pencils correctly.
Here are some photos of our learning and experiences in Autumn One.
Your child has now come home with a 'Learn to Read' book and a learning log. Our Learn to Read books cover the sounds we have been learning in school and some tricky words (common exception words). Please read at least three times per week with your child and record this in their learning log. Children who read three times per week are a 'regular reader' and will be invited to a reading reward at the end of each half term. The lovely Mrs Blewitt has recorded a video so you can see what reading at home should look like and this has been sent home on Tapestry.
Autumn two
What a busy half term it has been!
Our topic was 'Awesome Autumn'. We explored the seasonal changes happening in our environment and talked about what we noticed. We went on a leaf hunt around school and had a pumpkin day! We cut open the pumpkins to explore what was inside, planted our own pumpkin seeds and made pumpkin soup. It was very yummy!
We read the story 'The Scarecrow's Wedding'. We then had our own wedding ceremony where the children wore their fancy clothes and two pretended to get married. We then had a dance and the children ate a biscuit they had decorated.
The children were so excited to see snow! We put on our coats and wellies and headed straight outside. The children found frost and ice and caught snowflakes on their tongues. Some even tried to make snow angels! This also meant we could compare winter weather to autumn weather. We talked about what clothes we wear in the different seasons and how the trees change.
We had lots to celebrate this half term! We learned about Remembrance Day, Diwali and Children in Need. During our RE day we learned about why we celebrate Christmas and about the nativity story. We performed our own superb nativity show and visited our local church, St. Leonard's, for our Christmas service. Finally, we had a class party and festive lunch.
Spring one
This half term our topic has been 'Stomp and Roar, Here Come the Dinosaurs!'. It began with us finding an egg on the field. We thought about what might be inside and how we can take care of the egg. Eventually, it cracked open to reveal a baby dinosaur inside! We took care of the baby dinosaur carefully by making it nests and thinking of what it might eat. Then, we went outside and find real dinosaur bones hidden in our field! Our teachers phoned the museum who said we can take the bones inside for investigation. They later sent us a letter to confirm we had found bones belonging to a Sarcosaurus! We carefully laid the bones out and drew what we thought the rest of the skeleton might look like.
We have had lots to celebrate what with New Year and Lunar New Year!
Spring two
This half term our topic has been 'Traditional Tales'. We have enjoyed exploring the stories 'Goldilocks and the Three Bears', 'Jack and the Beanstalk', 'The Three Little Pigs', 'The Gingerbread Man' and 'The Billy Goat's Gruff'. Our topic began with us coming to school to find our home corners had been left in a big mess with oats and broken chairs. The children realised that Goldilocks must have been! We also grew our own beanstalks and explored the story of 'Jack and the Beanstalk'. Later, we found crumbs on our rugs in the morning so our teachers checked the camera's to see that the Gingerbread Man had been running away from Mr and Mrs Baker through our classrooms, the library and were seen outside the front of our school! We enjoyed exploring the Three Little Pigs and the children had a go at building houses with different materials to see which was strongest. They enjoyed pretending to be the Big Bad Wolf and trying to blow them down!
We have also had lots to celebrate! We loved our first World Book Day at school and walked to our local library in Lowford to listen to a special story and explore the books. We also learned about the festival of Eid and were really proud of our children who celebrate this with their families as they confidently shared their experiences with their class. We held a dress up day where the theme was 'Dress as what you would like to be when you are older'. This was to raise money to send to people in Uganda to help them receive an education and get a good job one day. Finally, we celebrated Easter with a visit to our local church St. Pauls. We listened carefully to the readings from our Head Boys and Girls as well as singing some songs we have been learning in our collective worship sessions.
